general_information.Learning-Teaching Method: - Offline/Online learning. - Project-Based Learning (PBL): An Integrated Export–Import Transaction Project is developed through staged milestones from opportunity identification to transaction completion, document-pack preparation, presentation, and individual defence. - Research-Based Learning (RBL): Students investigate product–market–partner opportunities, market-access conditions, buyer/supplier credibility, regulatory requirements, logistics options, and transaction risks using evidence from the textbook, official sources, and lecturer-approved datasets. - Applied learning methods include mini-lectures, transaction mapping, case analysis, numerical workshops, contract drafting, document-pack laboratories, simulations, peer review, project clinics, and professional defence.
general_information.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_information.Description: This course develops the applied knowledge and professional decision-making skills required to plan, execute, control, and evaluate international export–import transactions. The course follows an end-to-end transaction logic covering international trade conditions; product, market, buyer, supplier, and channel research; export pricing and import landed cost; Incoterms® 2020; international sales and channel agreements; transportation, freight forwarding, cargo insurance and claims; trade documents; foreign-exchange exposure; international payment and trade finance; export–import compliance; import regulations; customs entry, HS classification, customs valuation, rules of origin, tariffs and taxes; trade remedies; intellectual-property protection; and digital trade. The course integrates Project-Based Learning and Research-Based Learning through an Integrated Export–Import Transaction Project. Students progressively transform research evidence into a commercially and operationally coherent transaction plan, including costing, quotation, contract, logistics, insurance, payment, compliance, customs, and document-pack outputs. The course emphasizes evidence-based reasoning, cross-document consistency, risk control, ethical conduct, and the ability to present and defend professional decisions.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Attend at least 80% of contact slots to be eligible for the final examination. - Prepare assigned textbook sections, official references, cases, and worksheets before class. - Participate actively in discussion, calculation workshops, contract and document laboratories, simulations, peer review, and project clinics. - Complete three progress tests, all required individual/in-class tasks, and the Integrated Group Project according to the announced deadlines. - Maintain a traceable record of research evidence, assumptions, calculations, sources, project contributions, and document revisions. - Present and individually defend the group's transaction decisions and submitted evidence in Slots 19–20. - Comply with academic integrity, professional conduct, source-verification, and AI-disclosure requirements.
general_information.Tools: Internet; institutional LMS/FLM/Edunext; presentation software; spreadsheet software; word-processing software; official trade, customs, tariff, logistics, and legal databases; document templates; AI-supported learning tools as directed by the lecturer
general_information.Note: AI Policy: Generative AI and other digital tools may be used only as guided by the lecturer for idea generation, research planning, language refinement, document checking, scenario exploration, and learning support. Students must disclose AI use in assessed coursework, verify outputs against the textbook and authoritative sources, and remain fully responsible for accuracy, legality, originality, confidentiality, and professional judgment. AI use is not permitted in progress tests or the final examination unless explicitly authorized. PBL/RBL evidence and learning products: transaction brief; research evidence matrix; buyer/supplier due-diligence scorecard; channel or sourcing rationale; export-costing/import-landed-cost worksheet; formal quotation or pro forma invoice; Incoterms decision note; draft international sales/purchase contract; logistics and cargo-insurance plan; payment and trade-finance flow; customs and compliance checklist; document pack; risk register; incident-response memorandum; presentation; and individual defence. Central project inquiry: How can an exporter or importer design and execute a commercially viable, documentarily consistent, legally compliant, and risk-controlled international transaction for a selected product, partner, and market? ITU coding used in the Schedule: I = Introduce; T = Teach/Practice; U = Utilize/Integrate.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Analyze the international trade environment, trade agreements, market conditions, and product–market–partner information to identify and justify feasible export or import opportunities.
Calculate export prices and import landed costs, prepare commercial quotations, and select and justify appropriate Incoterms® 2020 rules and named places or ports for international transactions.

Draft and evaluate international sales or purchase contracts and selected channel agreements by applying relevant commercial principles, CISG fundamentals, and appropriate allocation of obligations, costs, risks, and remedies.
Design and evaluate transportation, freight-forwarding, cargo-insurance, and claims arrangements appropriate to the goods, route, delivery terms, and transaction risks.
Prepare and audit core export–import documents for accuracy, completeness, and consistency across contract, quotation, shipment, insurance, payment, and customs requirements.

Select and justify international payment, foreign-exchange risk-management, and trade-finance instruments, and identify documentary-credit discrepancies, fraud risks, and appropriate control measures.

Analyze and apply export–import compliance and customs requirements, including trade controls, HS classification, customs valuation, origin, tariffs and taxes, trade remedies, intellectual-property protection, and digital-trade requirements.

Develop, present, and defend an evidence-based, end-to-end export or import transaction project while demonstrating research capability, critical thinking, teamwork, professional communication, ethical judgment, and responsible use of digital and AI tools.

schedule.Student's Tasks: Before class: review HS structure. In class: classify typical goods at an introductory managerial level. After class: prepare the product-description and classification rationale.

schedule.Topic: 9.4 Customs valuation - Transaction value, additions, related-party issues, identical/similar goods, deductive value, computed value, and fallback method
schedule.Student Materials: Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 18; WTO Customs Valuation Agreement; valuation worksheet
schedule.Student's Tasks: Before class: review valuation hierarchy. In class: calculate customs value under sample scenarios. After class: document the valuation basis and evidence for the project.

schedule.Topic: 9.5 Rules of origin, preferential treatment, certificates of origin, and marking - Origin criteria, documentary proof, cumulation, direct consignment, and verification risk
schedule.Student Materials: Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapters 2, 16, and 18; VNTR/FTA origin references
schedule.Student's Tasks: Before class: review origin concepts. In class: assess preferential eligibility. After class: specify the origin evidence and unresolved verification risks.

schedule.Topic: 9.6 Import duties and taxes; customs broker and warehousing decisions; integrated customs compliance checklist
schedule.Student Materials: Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapters 16–18; customs-costing and compliance worksheets; IEI301 Integrated Transaction Project Brief and milestone worksheets
schedule.Student's Tasks: Before class: assemble tariff, value, origin, and tax inputs. In class: calculate duty/tax and audit customs readiness. After class: submit the project customs/compliance checkpoint.

schedule.Topic: UNIT 10. TRADE REMEDIES, ALTERNATIVE TRANSACTIONS, AND COURSE INTEGRATION 10.1 Anti-dumping, countervailing measures, and safeguards - Core concepts, material injury, business exposure, and early-warning response
schedule.Student Materials: Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 19; WTO trade-remedies resources
schedule.Student's Tasks: Before class: distinguish the three measures. In class: analyze a trade-remedy scenario. After class: prepare an early-warning and evidence-preservation plan.

schedule.Topic: 10.2 Countertrade and alternative transactions; integrated incident-response clinic - Barter, counterpurchase, buy-back, offsets, and response to payment, cargo, customs, or documentary failure
schedule.LO: CLO3, CLO4, CLO5, CLO6, CLO7, CLO8
schedule.Student Materials: Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 12 and integrated closing cases; IEI301 Integrated Transaction Project Brief and milestone worksheets
schedule.Student's Tasks: Before class: review alternative forms and the assigned incident. In class: design a response under constrained payment or transaction failure. After class: submit the risk-incident memorandum.

schedule.Topic: 10.3 Course integration, Progress Test 3, and final project readiness review - Scope: Units 7–10; end-to-end transaction coherence
schedule.Student Materials: Assigned materials from Sessions 34–53; project readiness checklist
schedule.Student's Tasks: Complete the individual closed-book Progress Test 3. After the test: finalize the project readiness checklist and personal defence preparation.
